facts.statement: The genus name Reesodus honors Jan Rees, who was the first to recognize the fossils as belonging to a distinct genus.
facts.quote: The generic name honors Jan Rees, who first realized that the fossils belong to a distinct genus.

facts.statement: Reesodus lived from the Tournaisian age of the Early Carboniferous to the Wordian age of the Permian.
facts.quote: It lived from the Tournaisian age of the Early Carboniferous to the Wordian age of the Permian

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Reesodus have been found in England, Russia, and Oman.
facts.quote: remains have been found in England, Russia and Oman

facts.statement: Reesodus is an extinct genus of hybodontiform fish.
facts.quote: Reesodus is an extinct genus of hybodontiform.

facts.statement: The genus Reesodus was established in 2013 as a replacement name for the previously unnamed 'Palaeozoic Genus 2'.
facts.quote: the genus Reesodus was erected in 2013 as a replacement name for 'Palaeozoic Genus 2'

facts.statement: Reesodus is classified as Hybodontiformes incertae sedis because its heterodonty pattern and potential enlarged lateral teeth cannot be assessed, though it is assumed to be close to the family Lonchidiidae.
facts.quote: Reesodus cannot be confidently assigned to any family (though it is assumed to be close to Lonchidiidae) as the heterodonty pattern and the possible presence of enlarged lateral teeth cannot be assessed, thus it is listed as Hybodontiformes incertae sedis.

facts.statement: The type species for the genus Reesodus is Reesodus underwoodi, which was described from the Khuff Formation of Oman.
facts.quote: the newly described Reesodus underwoodi from the Khuff Formation of Oman as the type species

facts.statement: The teeth of Reesodus underwoodi are small, symmetrical, and measure between 0.4 and 0.5 mm in height.
facts.quote: The teeth are small and symmetrical, measuring 0.4–0.5 mm high.

facts.statement: Reesodus pectinatus was originally described in 1996 as Lissodus pectinatus before being recognized as a separate genus.
facts.quote: Reesodus pectinatus was originally described in 1996 as Lissodus pectinatus, but has since been recognized to belong in this separate genus.

facts.statement: Reesodus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
The time range for Reesodus is from the Visean to the Wordian, spanning from 339.9 to 264.28 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Visean to Wordian (339.9 to 264.28 million years ago)
